agentCan: Implement the 3-legged authorization code flow and OIDC userinfo calls
Design the re-authorization loop for the 60-day token lifespan (no general refresh tokens)

approval.cost: The LinkedIn documentation read states no fee for creating an app, for Open Permissions, or for Marketing Developer Platform tiers
approval.trigger: Split by product family. Open Permissions need NO LinkedIn approval: they are 'the only permissions that are available to all developers without special approval', addable 'via self-service through the LinkedIn Developer Portal', and any LinkedIn member can then connect (no pre-approval user/install cap documented; documented throttles for the sign-in product are Member 500 requests/day, Application 100,000 requests/day). Everything else requires explicit approval: 'Most permissions and partner programs require explicit approval from LinkedIn.' Marketing Developer Platform: 'Developers seeking to build a marketing related integration using Advertising API permissions must be approved. You can apply for access through the Developer Portal.' Prerequisites include a verified Company Page, a verified business email ('Personal email addresses won't pass the review process'), organization legal name/address/website, and an app name that doesn't 'include any portion of the LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos'. Tiers: 'All applications start with Development tier. You must apply separately to upgrade to the Standard tier.' Advertising Development allows creating 1 test Ad Account and editing up to 5 ad accounts you administer; Standard is unlimited and requested via the Developer Portal settings / a support ticket, with a video demonstrating how your platform creates, edits and/or optimizes campaigns. Community Management Development caps all APIs at 500 calls per app per 24 hrs (100 per member; BATCH_GET not allowed; webhooks for social actions disabled); Standard has 'No restrictions', via a form, a screen recording of your app, and shared test credentials. 'LinkedIn reserves the right to review applications and select partners at its discretion and a partner might not be upgraded even if they meet these minimum requirements.' Restricted Marketing APIs (Matched Audiences, Audience Insights, Media Planning, Company Intelligence) require Advertising API access first for the first three; 'Matched Audiences API responses take up to 60 days' and LinkedIn contacts you only if it identifies a fit; 'Other restricted APIs are evaluated on a case-by-case basis with no fixed timeline.' Some permissions are closed outright: r_full_profile and r_member_social are closed permissions ('we are not accepting access requests'), and the Compliance permissions are 'for reference purposes only. Access is closed and may not be requested'.
approval.wait: Restricted APIs: Matched Audiences up to 60 days; others no fixed timeline. Advertising API initial approval and Standard-tier upgrades: not stated

blockers.detail: The standard 3-legged docs' 'Step 5: Refresh Access Token' is just re-running the authorization flow (silent only while the member is still logged in and the current token unexpired). True programmatic refresh tokens are gated: 'LinkedIn supports programmatic refresh tokens for all approved Marketing Developer Platform (MDP) partners', and the flow page notes they 'are available for a limited set of partners'. A generic SaaS must design for periodic user re-authorization every 60 days or less.
blockers.howToClear: Build a proactive re-authorization experience (warn before day 60), or pursue MDP partner approval if your use case fits marketing.
blockers.title: Refresh tokens are the exception, not the rule

blockers.detail: 'If you request a different scope than the previously granted scope, all the previous access tokens are invalidated', and 'If the scope permissions are changed in your app, your users must re-authenticate.' Consent is also all-or-nothing: 'If multiple scopes are requested, the user must be consent to all of them and may not select individual scopes', so request the minimum. (Multiple tokens with the SAME scope can coexist across clients.)
blockers.howToClear: Fix the scope set before launch and never change it casually.
blockers.title: Scope changes nuke existing tokens

blockers.detail: The app must be associated with a LinkedIn Company Page at creation, and 'Company Page Verification is one of the prerequisites for a developer application applying for access to a product. Do not use a fake company page... Ensure that a super admin of the LinkedIn Page associated with your organization has verified your developer application... Any failure to meet the above prerequisites will result in your access request being rejected.' The verifying super admin is often a different person than the developer.
blockers.howToClear: Secure the real Company Page and its super admin's verification before applying for any product.
blockers.title: The Company Page gate is a hard prerequisite

Two-legged auth is not available for marketing use cases.').

alternatives: Application Authentication (2-legged / client credentials): exists for some partner permissions (e.g. some Sales Navigator Application Platform permissions are marked 'Application Auth'), but not for Marketing and not a general consumer option
flavor.recommended: The 3-legged Authorization Code Flow (Member Authentication) on an app carrying only Open-Permission products: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect, plus Share on LinkedIn if users must post as themselves
flavor.why: The object is an app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal (linkedin.com/developers > My Apps), mandatorily associated with a LinkedIn Company Page at creation. Capabilities come not from the app itself but from Products added under the app's Products tab: 'LinkedIn products can be enabled after creating a new application.' Each product provisions specific OAuth permissions (scopes), visible under the app's Auth tab alongside the Client ID and Primary Client Secret. Open products: Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect (scopes openid, profile: 'Retrieve authenticated member's name, headline, and photo', email: 'Retrieve authenticated member's primary email address') and Share on LinkedIn (w_member_social: 'Post, comment and like posts on behalf of an authenticated member'). Requesting openid returns an ID token (JWT, RS256; validate via the discovery document / JWKS); member details are also at GET api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo. Two cautions from the docs: 'Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect does not verify user identities and should not be marketed as such', and the discovery document shows subject_types_supported ['pairwise'] (the sub identifier is per-client).

humanMust: Have a LinkedIn account and a real LinkedIn Company Page for your organization
Create the app (name, associated Page, logo, privacy policy URL, legal agreement)
Get the app verified: generate the verification URL in Settings and have a super admin of the associated Page open it and confirm responsibility
Add Products under the Products tab (Open Permissions self-service; partner products submit an access-request form)
Configure the Auth tab: copy the Client ID and Primary Client Secret; register Authorized redirect URLs
name: LinkedIn
nuances: Programmatic refresh tokens (approved MDP partners only): 'By default, access tokens are valid for 60 days and programmatic refresh tokens are valid for a year', but the refresh token's TTL is fixed at issuance and does NOT extend on use: 'Day 360, If you generate a new access token, your access token and refresh token will both expire in 5 days... and you must get your application reauthorized by the member.' Also: 'LinkedIn reserves the right to revoke Refresh Tokens or Access Tokens at any time due to technical or policy reasons.'

Authorization codes have a '30-minute lifespan and must be used immediately'. Access tokens are '~500 characters. We recommend that you plan for your application to handle tokens with length of at least 1000 characters' (both access and refresh tokens). Redirect URL rules: 'URLs must be absolute' (query parameters are ignored) and a URL 'cannot include a # fragment'. If a grant already exists, 'the authorization screen is bypassed and the member is immediately redirected'.

Roles, not just scopes: for organization/ad data 'members must have the appropriate roles as defined in Company Page Roles and Ad Account Roles' (e.g. rw_organization_admin requires the member to be an ADMINISTRATOR of the organization; rw_ads requires one of ACCOUNT_BILLING_ADMIN, ACCOUNT_MANAGER, CAMPAIGN_MANAGER, CREATIVE_MANAGER).

Development-tier clocks: for Community Management, 'You must complete your integration and testing within twelve months of receiving the API access'; if you don't apply for Standard within twelve months, 'we'll remove your API access due to inactivity'. Legacy surface is deprecated: the old Sign In scopes (r_liteprofile, r_emailaddress) are superseded by the OIDC product; in Marketing, r_ads_leadgen_automation 'was deprecated in July 2023' and rw_offlineConversions 'was deprecated in October 2023'; Marketing API versions sunset on a schedule.

Some use cases are flatly not approved: 'Can I create a social feed display with your APIs? No, displaying a company page feed on your website or any other digital channel off LinkedIn is not an approved use case.' In OIDC userinfo, email and email_verified 'are optional and may not be included in all responses'.

App logo and privacy policy URL
For partner products: a verified business email, organization legal name/address/website

steps.detail: The app must be associated with a Page. Create the app in the Developer Portal: app name, the LinkedIn Page to associate, app logo, privacy policy URL, accept the legal agreement.
steps.title: Create the app (Company Page required)

steps.detail: In the app's Settings, generate the verification URL; a super admin of the associated Page must open it and confirm responsibility for the app. Skipping this gets product access requests rejected.
steps.title: Verify the app via the Page super admin

steps.detail: 'Select your app from My Apps, navigate to the Products tab, and request the Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect product.' Open Permissions are self-service; partner products submit an access-request form for LinkedIn review. Then configure the Auth tab: Client ID and Primary Client Secret, and register Authorized redirect URLs (absolute, no # fragment).

links.label: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect

steps.title: Add Products; configure the Auth tab

steps.detail: GET linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri (must match a registered URL), state (CSRF), scope. Exchange the code (30-minute lifespan) at POST linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken (form-encoded: grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri). Access tokens have a 60-day lifespan (expires_in 5184000).
steps.title: Run the 3-legged flow

steps.detail: Authorization: Bearer against api.linkedin.com/v2 (e.g. /v2/me, or /v2/userinfo for OIDC; validate the ID token via the JWKS if you requested openid).
steps.title: Call the API

steps.detail: There is no general refresh token. Before the 60 days lapse, re-run the authorization flow (silent if the member is still logged in and the token hasn't expired). Only approved Marketing Developer Platform partners get programmatic refresh tokens (365-day fixed TTL).
steps.title: Maintain the connection (re-authorization, not refresh)

steps.detail: Advertising API and Community Management API each have their own application; Development tier first (Community Management: 500 calls/app/24 hrs; Advertising: 1 test Ad Account, edits on up to 5 administered accounts), then a separate Standard-tier application (form, screen recording, test credentials / demo video). Restricted APIs sit behind Advertising API access with responses up to 60 days.
steps.time: Up to 60 days for restricted APIs; other durations not stated
steps.title: (Marketing only) Apply for partner access and the Standard tier

tagline: An app tied to a verified Company Page, where identity and sharing are self-service Open Permissions but there are no general refresh tokens (60-day tokens, then re-authorize), and everything beyond that is an approval-gated partner program with Development and Standard tiers.

time.active: ~40 min of portal setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day for Open Permissions; partner approvals range from unstated to up to 60 days (restricted APIs)
